server_intro: is the self-hosted version of GitHub Enterprise. It is installed on-premises or on a private cloud and provides organizations with a secure and customizable source code management and collaboration platform.
server_control: One of the key advantages of GitHub Enterprise Server is that it provides organizations with complete control over their source code and data. Organizations can choose where to store their repositories and can control who has access to them. Administrators can also customize the platform to meet specific needs, such as integrating other tools or implementing custom workflows.
server_compliance: GitHub Enterprise Server also offers enhanced security and compliance features. Organizations can configure their instance to meet their specific security requirements, such as using LDAP or SAML for authentication, setting up two-factor authentication, or implementing network security measures. Compliance features are also included, such as audit logs, access controls, and vulnerability scanning.
security_intro: GitHub Enterprise is designed with security in mind and includes a range of features to help organizations protect their code and data. Here are some of the key security features that GitHub Enterprise offers:
security_authentication: Authentication and access controls: GitHub Enterprise includes two-factor authentication, LDAP and Active Directory integration, and OAuth authentication. This helps organizations ensure that only authorized users can access their repositories and data.
security_encryption: Encryption: All data in transit between the user's computer and GitHub Enterprise server is encrypted using HTTPS. All data at rest uses AES-256 encryption.
security_scanning: Vulnerability scanning: GitHub Enterprise includes built-in security scanning features that can detect known vulnerabilities and alert users.
security_audit: Audit logs: The platform provides detailed audit logs that record all user actions, including repository access, changes, and deletions. This helps organizations track and monitor user activity and identify potential security issues.
security_policies: Customizable policies: GitHub Enterprise allows organizations to create custom policies for repository access. This can help enforce compliance requirements and prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data.
security_updates: Regular security updates: There is also a dedicated security team that provides regular updates, monitors for potential security threats, and responds quickly to any issues that arise.

selection_question: What are you looking for? Who decides who is selected?
selection_answer: All of our applications will be thoroughly evaluated by a selection committee. You'll be much more likely to be selected if you:
selection_users: Have an active and growing set of users
selection_growth: Understand how you want to grow and maintain your project
selection_fulltime: Wish to pursue open source work full-time
benefits_question: What do I get if I'm selected?
benefits_stipend: $20,000 stipend per person ($2,000 per week of participation) for the duration of the 10 week program.
benefits_mentors: Dedicated mentors from the open source community and enterprises
duties_question: What do I have to do if I'm selected?
duties_participation: Participate in all Accelerator activities during the 10-week program (roughly 10 hours per week)
duties_resources: Contribute to the open source resources we have on GitHub so other developers can learn from your experience
dates_question: What are the exact dates of the program? What does Winter 2023 mean?
dates_answer: The program applications are due by December 31, 2022. We will announce the first class of fellows on February 15, 2023. The program itself will run from March 6, 2023 to May 12, 2023.

codespace_answer: A codespace is a development environment hosted in the cloud. You can customize your GitHub Codespaces project by configuring dev container files in your repository (known as configuration-as-code). This creates a repeatable codespace configuration for all users of your project.
heading: Frequently asked questions
github_startups_offer: What's included in the GitHub for Startups offer?
github_startups_offer_answer: All GitHub for Startups companies receive up to 20 seats of GitHub Enterprise for free for year one and 50% off year two. Learn more about the features and capabilities of GitHub Enterprise
who_eligible_answer: Startups who meet the following criteria are eligible to apply for the program:
must_be_associated: Must be associated with a current GitHub for Startups partner.
not_current_customer: Not a current GitHub Enterprise customer
no_previous_credits: Must not have previously received credits for GitHub Enterprise
startup_not_eligible: What if my startup is not eligible? Are there other resources for me?
